title: The Digital Web
summary: A realm of thought built by mages' will and reached through computers.

claims.text: The Digital Web, or Net, has no physical form; it exists in mages' minds, threaded through every plane as strands of unformed Pattern.
Some say the strands are tied to the Weaver and join every piece of high-tech electronics.
A mage projects consciousness in through a computer and, with enough skill, can shape empty Web into a personal space and invite others in.

title: The Adepts' break with the Union
summary: How Virtual Adepts turned computers toward the Masses.

claims.text: Technocratic backing let Dr. Bell found a company, and research into switches for the telephone network led to vacuum tubes and transistors.
The Union set the Virtual Adepts to build the first electric computers under brutal deadlines; sickened by the World War, the Adepts took free information to the Masses instead.

title: Restricted sectors
summary: Sealed-off parts of the Digital Web.

claims.text: Technocratic zones look like sharp, pixelated geometry, patrolled by killer programs and Union agents.
Syndicate corporate networks and NWO government and phone systems are sealed, as are Virtual Adept Chantries; Iteration X has closed every route to Autochthonia.

title: The Spy's Demise
summary: A neutral club in the Net where even Technocrats are welcome.

claims.text: The Demise is a standing truce zone in the Ascension War, open to Tradition and Technocracy mages alike.
Conduits from nearly every grid sector feed Sleeper chat rooms into it; patrons spy on those rooms, and the staff turn the Quintessence Sleepers spend online into Tass drinks.
Its Cathedral room, said to be the work of a Celestial Chorus mage, hosts debates between Tradition and Technocracy on God and Ascension.
